shlokas.sanskrit: एतदाख्याय काकुत्स्थो भ्रातृभ्याममितप्रभः । लक्ष्मणं पुनरेवाह धर्मयुक्तमिदं वचः ।। 7.91.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: etadākhyāya kākutstho bhrātṛbhyāmamitaprabhaḥ | lakṣmaṇaṃ punarevāha dharmayuktamidaṃ vacaḥ || 7.91.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having narrated this, Kakutstha of measureless splendor spoke once more to his two brothers, addressing to Lakshmana these words that were in accord with dharma:

shlokas.sanskrit: वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ कश्यपम् । द्विजांश्च सर्वप्रवरानश्वमेधपुरस्कृतान् ।। 7.91.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vasiṣṭhaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca jābālimatha kaśyapam | dvijāṃśca sarvapravarānaśvamedhapuraskṛtān || 7.91.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Having assembled Vasishtha and Vamadeva, and Jabali and Kashyapa, and all the foremost of the twice-born who hold the horse-sacrifice in highest regard,

shlokas.sanskrit: एतान्सर्वान्समानीय मन्त्रयित्वा च लक्ष्मण । हयं लक्षणसम्पन्नं विमोक्ष्यामि समाधिना ।। 7.91.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: etānsarvānsamānīya mantrayitvā ca lakṣmaṇa | hayaṃ lakṣaṇasampannaṃ vimokṣyāmi samādhinā || 7.91.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: having gathered all these together and taken counsel with them, O Lakshmana, I shall, with due rite, release a horse endowed with the proper marks."

shlokas.sanskrit: तद्वाक्यं राघवेणोक्तं श्रुत्वा त्वरितविक्रमः । द्विजान्सर्वान्समाहूय दर्शयामास राघवम् ।। 7.91.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tadvākyaṃ rāghaveṇoktaṃ śrutvā tvaritavikramaḥ | dvijānsarvānsamāhūya darśayāmāsa rāghavam || 7.91.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing that word spoken by Raghava, he of swift valor summoned all the twice-born and presented them to Raghava.

shlokas.sanskrit: ते दृष्ट्वा देवसङ्काशं कृतपादाभिवन्दनम् । राघवं सुदुराधर्षमाशीर्भिः समपूजयन् ।। 7.91.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te dṛṣṭvā devasaṅkāśaṃ kṛtapādābhivandanam | rāghavaṃ sudurādharṣamāśīrbhiḥ samapūjayan || 7.91.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Beholding Raghava, who resembled a god and was most unassailable, they made obeisance at his feet and honored him with their blessings.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्राञ्जलिः स तदा भूत्वा राघवो द्विजसत्तमान् । आचचक्षे ऽश्वमेधस्य ह्यभिप्रायं महायशाः ।। 7.91.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: prāñjaliḥ sa tadā bhūtvā rāghavo dvijasattamān | ācacakṣe 'śvamedhasya hyabhiprāyaṃ mahāyaśāḥ || 7.91.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the greatly renowned Raghava, folding his hands in reverence, declared to those best of the twice-born his intention concerning the horse-sacrifice.

shlokas.sanskrit: ते तु रामस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा नमस्कृत्वा वृषध्वजम् । अश्वमेधं द्विजाः सर्वे पूजयन्ति स्म सर्वशः ।। 7.91.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te tu rāmasya tacchrutvā namaskṛtvā vṛṣadhvajam | aśvamedhaṃ dvijāḥ sarve pūjayanti sma sarvaśaḥ || 7.91.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And having heard that from Rama, all those twice-born ones, bowing to the bull-bannered god, praised the horse-sacrifice in every way.

shlokas.sanskrit: स तेषां द्विजमुख्यानां वाक्यमद्भुतदर्शनम् । अश्वमेधाश्रितं श्रुत्वा भृशं प्रीतो ऽभवत्तदा ।। 7.91.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa teṣāṃ dvijamukhyānāṃ vākyamadbhutadarśanam | aśvamedhāśritaṃ śrutvā bhṛśaṃ prīto 'bhavattadā || 7.91.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing the wondrous-seeming words of those chief among the twice-born, words bearing upon the horse-sacrifice, he became exceedingly pleased then.

shlokas.sanskrit: विज्ञाय कर्म तत्तेषां रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् । प्रेषयस्व द्रुतं दूतान् सुग्रीवाय महात्मने ।। 7.91.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vijñāya karma tatteṣāṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt | preṣayasva drutaṃ dūtān sugrīvāya mahātmane || 7.91.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Understanding the resolve of those ones, Rama said to Lakshmana: "Send messengers swiftly to the great-souled Sugriva."

shlokas.sanskrit: यथा महद्भिर्हरिभिर्बहुभिश्च वनौकसाम् । सार्धमागच्छ भद्रं ते ह्यनुभोक्तुं महोत्सवम् ।। 7.91.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yathā mahadbhirharibhirbahubhiśca vanaukasām | sārdhamāgaccha bhadraṃ te hyanubhoktuṃ mahotsavam || 7.91.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Come together with the many great vanaras, the forest-dwellers, that you may partake of this great festival; may good befall you.

shlokas.sanskrit: बिभीषणश्च रक्षोभिः कामगैर्बहुभिर्वृतः । अश्वमेधं महायज्ञमायात्वतुलविक्रमः ।। 7.91.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bibhīṣaṇaśca rakṣobhiḥ kāmagairbahubhirvṛtaḥ | aśvamedhaṃ mahāyajñamāyātvatulavikramaḥ || 7.91.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And let Vibhishana of unequalled valour, surrounded by his many rakshasas who travel at will, come to the great sacrifice, the horse-sacrifice.

shlokas.sanskrit: राजानश्च महाभागा ये मे प्रियचिकीर्षवः । सानुगाः क्षिप्रमायान्तु यज्ञं द्रष्टुमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.91.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rājānaśca mahābhāgā ye me priyacikīrṣavaḥ | sānugāḥ kṣipramāyāntu yajñaṃ draṣṭumanuttamam || 7.91.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And let the illustrious kings who wish to do me a kindness come quickly with their retinues to witness this most excellent sacrifice.

shlokas.sanskrit: देशान्तरगता ये च द्विजा धर्मसमाहिताः । आमन्त्रयस्व तान्सर्वानश्वमेधाय लक्ष्मण ।। 7.91.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: deśāntaragatā ye ca dvijā dharmasamāhitāḥ | āmantrayasva tānsarvānaśvamedhāya lakṣmaṇa || 7.91.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And those brahmins who, devoted to dharma, have gone away to other lands — invite them all to the horse-sacrifice, O Lakshmana.

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋषयश्च महाबाहो आहूयन्तां तपोधनाः । देशान्तरगताः सर्वे सदाराश्च द्विजातयः । तथैव तालावचरास्तथैव नटनर्तकाः ।। 7.91.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ṛṣayaśca mahābāho āhūyantāṃ tapodhanāḥ | deśāntaragatāḥ sarve sadārāśca dvijātayaḥ | tathaiva tālāvacarāstathaiva naṭanartakāḥ || 7.91.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And let the sages rich in austerity be summoned, O mighty-armed one, and all the twice-born brahmins who have gone to other lands, together with their wives, and likewise those who keep time with poles, and likewise the actors and dancers.

shlokas.sanskrit: यज्ञवाटश्च सुमहान्गोमत्या नैमिशे वने । आज्ञाप्यतां महाबाहो तद्धि पुण्यमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.91.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yajñavāṭaśca sumahāngomatyā naimiśe vane | ājñāpyatāṃ mahābāho taddhi puṇyamanuttamam || 7.91.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And let a very great sacrificial enclosure be commanded to be made by the Gomati in the Naimisha forest, O mighty-armed one, for that is most holy and supremely meritorious.

shlokas.sanskrit: शान्तयश्च महाबाहो प्रवर्त्यन्तां समन्ततः ।। 7.91.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śāntayaśca mahābāho pravartyantāṃ samantataḥ || 7.91.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And let the propitiatory rites be set in motion on every side, O mighty-armed one.

shlokas.sanskrit: शतशश्चापि धर्मज्ञाः क्रतुमुख्यमनुत्तमम् । अनुभूय महायज्ञं नैमिशे रघुनन्दन ।। 7.91.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śataśaścāpi dharmajñāḥ kratumukhyamanuttamam | anubhūya mahāyajñaṃ naimiśe raghunandana || 7.91.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And hundreds of those learned in dharma, having partaken of the great sacrifice, the foremost and most excellent of rites, at Naimisha, O delight of the Raghus —

shlokas.sanskrit: तुष्टः पुष्टश्च सर्वो ऽसौ मानितश्च यथाविधि । प्रीतिं यास्यति धर्मज्ञ शीघ्रमामन्त्र्यतां जनः ।। 7.91.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaśca sarvo 'sau mānitaśca yathāvidhi | prītiṃ yāsyati dharmajña śīghramāmantryatāṃ janaḥ || 7.91.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: — every one of them, satisfied and well-nourished and honoured according to the proper rites, will attain to gladness, O knower of dharma; so let the people be invited quickly.

shlokas.sanskrit: शतं वाहसहस्राणां तण्डुलानां वपुष्मताम् । अयुतं तिलमुद्गानां प्रयात्वग्रे महाबल ।। 7.91.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śataṃ vāhasahasrāṇāṃ taṇḍulānāṃ vapuṣmatām | ayutaṃ tilamudgānāṃ prayātvagre mahābala || 7.91.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Let a hundred thousand cartloads of fine, plump rice grains, and ten thousand of sesame and mung beans, go on ahead, O mighty one.

shlokas.sanskrit: चणकानां कुलित्थानां माषाणां लवणस्य च । अतो ऽनुरूपं स्नेहं च गन्धं सङ्क्षिप्तमेव च ।। 7.91.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: caṇakānāṃ kulitthānāṃ māṣāṇāṃ lavaṇasya ca | ato 'nurūpaṃ snehaṃ ca gandhaṃ saṅkṣiptameva ca || 7.91.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And of chickpeas, of horse-gram, of black gram, and of salt, and a fitting quantity of oil and fragrant substances, all duly gathered.

shlokas.sanskrit: सुवर्णकोट्यो बहुला हिरण्यस्य शतोत्तराः । अग्रतो भरतः कृत्वा गच्छत्वग्रे समाधिना ।। 7.91.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: suvarṇakoṭyo bahulā hiraṇyasya śatottarāḥ | agrato bharataḥ kṛtvā gacchatvagre samādhinā || 7.91.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Many tens of millions of pieces of gold, and of silver more than a hundred times that — let Bharata, placing these at the head, go on ahead with concentrated attention.

shlokas.sanskrit: अन्तरा पण्यवीथ्यश्च सर्वे च नटनर्तकाः । सूदा नार्यश्च बहवो नित्यं यौवनशालिनः ।। 7.91.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: antarā paṇyavīthyaśca sarve ca naṭanartakāḥ | sūdā nāryaśca bahavo nityaṃ yauvanaśālinaḥ || 7.91.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And in between let there be rows of market-stalls, and all the actors and dancers, the cooks, and many women ever radiant with youth.

shlokas.sanskrit: भरतेन तु सार्धं ते यान्तु सैन्यानि चाग्रतः । नैगमा बलवृद्धाश्च द्विजाश्च सुसमाहिताः ।। 7.91.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bharatena tu sārdhaṃ te yāntu sainyāni cāgrataḥ | naigamā balavṛddhāśca dvijāśca susamāhitāḥ || 7.91.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And together with Bharata let the armies march in the van, and the townsmen, those advanced in strength, and the well-composed brahmins.

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्मान्तिकान्वर्धकिनः कोशाध्यक्षांश्च नैगमान् । मम मातऽस्तथा सर्वाः कुमारान्तःपुराणि च ।। 7.91.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: karmāntikānvardhakinaḥ kośādhyakṣāṃśca naigamān | mama māta'stathā sarvāḥ kumārāntaḥpurāṇi ca || 7.91.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: The labourers, the carpenters, the overseers of the treasury, and the townsfolk, and likewise all my mothers and the princes and the women of the inner apartments —

shlokas.sanskrit: काञ्चनीं मम पत्नीं च दीक्षायां ज्ञांश्च कर्मणि । अग्रतो भरतः कृत्वा गच्छत्वग्रे महायशाः ।। 7.91.25 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kāñcanīṃ mama patnīṃ ca dīkṣāyāṃ jñāṃśca karmaṇi | agrato bharataḥ kṛtvā gacchatvagre mahāyaśāḥ || 7.91.25 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: — and my golden consort, made for the consecration, and those skilled in the rites — placing Bharata at the head, let the greatly renowned one go on ahead.

shlokas.sanskrit: उपकार्या महार्हाश्च पार्थिवानां महौजसाम् । सानुगानां नरश्रेष्ठो व्यादिदेश महाबलः ।। 7.91.26 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: upakāryā mahārhāśca pārthivānāṃ mahaujasām | sānugānāṃ naraśreṣṭho vyādideśa mahābalaḥ || 7.91.26 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the costly and worthy lodging-pavilions for the mighty and powerful kings together with their retinues — these the foremost of men, the one of great strength, commanded to be prepared.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 91 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe ekanavatitamaḥ sargaḥ || 91 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the ninety-first sarga in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the sacred Ramayana, the first poem, composed by the sage Valmiki.
